unit.title: Как работает игровой цикл: ввод, обновление и отрисовка

learning_outcomes.statement: Names the three phases of the game loop (Input -> Update -> Render), explains why their order is not arbitrary, and catalogues the two classic first-loop bugs.

evidence.summary: Learning objective and scope: Names the three phases of the game loop (Input -> Update -> Render), explains why their order is not arbitrary, and catalogues the two classic first-loop bugs.

Input must precede Update and Update must precede Render, or the game reacts or draws one frame late. -- Confirmed -- the reasoning is correct and is the same mechanism behind the 20.23 animation-lag bug, which the section cross-references.

Skipping `pygame.init()` leaves some modules uninitialised, and the resulting error often points at a different line. -- Confirmed exactly -- without init(), `mixer.Sound(...)` raises `pygame.error: mixer not initialized` and `font.SysFont(...)` raises `pygame.error: font not initialized`, while `display.set_mode()` silently succeeds. Sound is indeed the first thing to break.
An unserviced event queue makes the OS mark the window 'Not responding'. -- Confirmed as accurate OS behaviour and consistent with the 20.28 symptom table.

Larger engines use more complex schemes (fixed physics timestep, split update phases, interpolation, threads). -- Confirmed -- an accurate, appropriately scoped caveat that stops the three-phase model being mistaken for the only model.
